pages.text: Rain poured through the night. Thunder boomed. Kota hid beneath the quilt and covered their ears.
A young frog asked Kota to play. "The sky's angry," Kota said, their voice muffled by the quilt.
Another crash made Kota tremble. "But rain is fun," the frog said.
Dad listened. "It's moving farther away. Let's count after each flash." Kota peeked out.
FLASH! "One, two, three!" At three came the thunder. Kota was too busy counting to hide.
Another flash. "One, two, three, four, five!" The wait was longer. The thunder was farther away.
At the next flash, Kota counted all the way to eight. A quiet rumble came from beyond the mountain. Kota kicked off the quilt, tail up.
All three listened to the rain at the window. The frog pressed a palm to the glass. "Ribbit, ribbit!" Kota copied, no longer afraid.
On the next rainy night, Kota sat straight on the quilt and counted on their fingers. "Flash! One, two!" As the counts grew longer, their shoulders straightened.
Dad rested a hand on Kota's head at bedtime. "Counting made the scary sound smaller." The rain sounded like a lullaby.
